literal: In recognition of his former merit in defending Jin Province, his offices and noble ranks were restored, and he was again appointed Minister of the Palace Guards.
idiomatic: In recognition of his earlier merit in holding Jin Province, his offices and noble ranks were restored, and he was again appointed minister of the palace guards.

literal: At that time the Mountain Hu raided and harassed Jin Province; Xiuyi was dispatched to pursue and suppress them, and he broke them.
idiomatic: At that time the Mountain Hu raided Jin Province; Xiuyi was sent in pursuit, broke them, and drove them off.

literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Zhengping Commandery, with the seal of opening an office conferred.
idiomatic: His rank was advanced to duke of Zhengping Commandery, and he was given the seal of opening an office.

literal: Emperor Shizong, following the Grand Ancestor's dying charge, reduced his fief by two hundred households and separately enfeoffed Xiuyi as Baron of Pingxiang.
idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, honoring the Grand Ancestor's dying charge, reduced the fief by two hundred households and separately enfeoffed Xiuyi as baron of Pingxiang.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was appointed protector of the army, separately enfeoffed Duke of Lantian County, and also made grand tutor of the crown prince.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed protector of the army, separately enfeoffed duke of Lantian County, and also made grand tutor of the crown prince.

literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year he died, aged seventy-seven.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year he died, aged seventy-seven.

literal: Posthumously granted military affairs of the three provinces of Jin, Tai, and Hua, Minister of Works, and governor of Jin Province, with three hundred bolts of goods given in tribute.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted military affairs over Jin, Tai, and Hua provinces, minister of works, and governor of Jin Province, with three hundred bolts of goods sent in tribute.

literal: His son Wenshu succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Wenshu succeeded.

literal: Xue Jiazu
idiomatic: Xue Jiazu

literal: Xiuyi's younger cousin Jiazu was likewise bold and forthright in nature.
idiomatic: Xiuyi's younger cousin Jiazu was likewise bold and open-handed in temperament.

literal: Upon first taking office he was made supernumerary Gentleman-Attendant at the Dispersal of Horses, and was gradually promoted to governor of Zhengping.
idiomatic: Upon first taking office he was made supernumerary gentleman-attendant at the dispersal of horses, and was gradually promoted to governor of Zhengping.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor was at Xindu, Jiazu heard and came to join the righteous cause.
idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor raised the cause at Xindu, Jiazu heard of it and came to join him.

literal: He followed in pacifying the Four Huns at Hanling and was appointed governor of Hua Province.
idiomatic: He followed in the victory over the Four Huns at Hanling and was appointed governor of Hua Province.

literal: When Heba Yue defied orders, Jiazu was ordered to post cavalry along the river to oppose the great army.
idiomatic: When Heba Yue defied orders, Jiazu was ordered to post cavalry along the river to hold back the main force.

literal: Jiazu thereupon abandoned his riding horse, crossed the river by swimming, and returned to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: Jiazu thereupon abandoned his mount, swam the river, and returned to the Grand Ancestor.

literal: Because of this he was appointed governor of Yang Province and died in office.
idiomatic: For this he was appointed governor of Yang Province and died in office.

literal: His son Zhen, styled Wenhun.
idiomatic: His son Zhen, styled Wenhun.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he received orders to garrison Longmen and was lost to Western Wei.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he received orders to hold Longmen and was taken by Western Wei.

literal: During Yuanxiang he was able to escape and return.
idiomatic: During Yuanxiang he at last escaped and returned.

literal: The Grand Ancestor praised his utmost loyalty and appointed him governor of Guang Province.
idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor praised his steadfast loyalty and appointed him governor of Guang Province.

literal: Later he followed Murong Shaozong in campaigning against Hou Jing and, for merit, was separately enfeoffed Baron of Fushi County.
idiomatic: Later he followed Murong Shaozong against Hou Jing and, for merit, was separately enfeoffed baron of Fushi County.

literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao, he followed in suppressing the Mountain Hu and breaking the Rouran, all with recorded merit, and was successively promoted to governor of Qiao Province.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianbao he followed campaigns against the Mountain Hu and the Rouran, winning merit in both, and was promoted in stages to governor of Qiao Province.

literal: Xue Yuanying
idiomatic: Xue Yuanying

literal: Xiuyi's nephew Yuanying — his father Guangchi was governor of Eastern Yong Province and minister of imperial sacrifices.
idiomatic: Xiuyi's nephew Yuanying; his father Guangchi had been governor of Eastern Yong Province and minister of imperial sacrifices.

literal: Yuanying was incorruptible, cautious, and trustworthy; he first took office as aide to the Prince of Yong'an.
idiomatic: Yuanying was incorruptible, careful, and trustworthy; he first entered service as aide to the Prince of Yong'an.

literal: Acting in the affairs of Xiurong County, he earned a reputation for integrity.
idiomatic: While acting in the affairs of Xiurong County, he won a name for clean government.

literal: After successive transfers he became vice-governor of Ding Province; recommended for integrity, fairness, and diligence, he was appointed governor of Yuyang.
idiomatic: After successive transfers he became vice-governor of Ding Province; recommended for integrity, fairness, and diligence, he was appointed governor of Yuyang.

literal: Chi Lieping
idiomatic: Chi Lieping

literal: Chi Lieping, styled Shagui, was a man of the western part of Dai Commandery; his family for generations were tribal chieftains.
idiomatic: Chi Lieping, styled Shagui — Slayer of Demons — was a man of western Dai Commandery; his family had been tribal chieftains for generations.

literal: Ping had a striking appearance, with a fine beard and mustache, and excelled at horsemanship and archery.
idiomatic: Ping was striking to look upon, with a handsome beard and mustache, and excelled at horsemanship and archery.

literal: He inherited the post of first tribally enrolled chieftain and the title Baron of Linjiang.
idiomatic: He inherited the post of first tribally enrolled chieftain and the title baron of Linjiang.

literal: At the end of Xiaochang, Balang rebelled; Rouran remnant forces invaded Mayi; Ping served as a subordinate army commander, had battle merit, and was appointed separate commander.
idiomatic: At the end of Xiaochang, Balang rebelled and Rouran remnant bands raided Mayi; Ping served under the army commander, won distinction in battle, and was appointed separate commander.

literal: Later Muzhi raised disorder; Liu Hulu and Hulu Kenali both at the same time plotted rebellion; Ping was made area commander to suppress and settle Hulu and the others.
idiomatic: Later Muzhi stirred rebellion; Liu Hulu and Hulu Kenali rose together; Ping was made area commander to suppress Hulu and the rest.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei's reign, he was appointed General of Martial Guards.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei's reign he was appointed general of martial guards.

literal: He followed Erzhu Rong in breaking Ge Rong and pacifying Yuan Hao, was transferred to commander of the central army and right guard general, enfeoffed Baron of Yingtao County with a fief of seven hundred households.
idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Rong in breaking Ge Rong and pacifying Yuan Hao, was transferred to commander of the central army and right guard general, and enfeoffed baron of Yingtao County with a fief of seven hundred households.

literal: When Rong died, Ping fled north together with Rong's wife and Erzhu Shilong and others.
idiomatic: When Rong died, Ping fled north with Rong's wife and Erzhu Shilong and the others.

literal: When Prince Changguang Ye was enthroned, he was appointed right guard general and additionally made grand commander of the capital region.
idiomatic: When Prince Changguang Ye was enthroned, he was appointed right guard general and additionally made grand commander of the capital region.

literal: At that time the Erzhu clan acted above their station; Ping often feared calamity; when the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous cause, Ping thereupon pledged his loyalty.
idiomatic: At that time the Erzhu clan overreached; Ping lived in constant fear of ruin; when the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous cause, Ping pledged himself to him.

literal: He followed in pacifying Ye and breaking the Four Huns at Hanling.
idiomatic: He followed in the pacification of Ye and the breaking of the Four Huns at Hanling.

literal: After Zhongyuan had fled, Ping was made chief commissioner of the Eastern Commandery circuit.
idiomatic: After Zhongyuan fled, Ping was made chief commissioner of the Eastern Commandery circuit.

literal: When the army returned, he followed the Grand Ancestor in pacifying Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: When the army returned, he followed the Grand Ancestor in pacifying Erzhu Zhao.

literal: Again he followed the army commander Lou Zhao in campaigning against and pacifying Fan Zihu.
idiomatic: Again he followed the army commander Lou Zhao in campaigning against Fan Zihu and pacifying him.

literal: He was granted bearer of the staff of authority and made governor of Hua Province.
idiomatic: He was granted bearer of the staff of authority and made governor of Hua Province.

literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Ping followed the Grand Ancestor in defeating Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Ping followed the Grand Ancestor in defeating Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang.

literal: At the beginning of Wuding, he was appointed governor of Kuo Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuding he was appointed governor of Kuo Province.

literal: In the fifth year he was given the rank equal to the Three Excellencies and garrisoned Heyang.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he was given rank equal to the three excellencies and garrisoned Heyang.

literal: In the eighth year his noble rank was advanced to marquis.
idiomatic: In the eighth year his noble rank was advanced to marquis.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was appointed governor of Yan Province; soon given the seal of opening an office and separately enfeoffed Viscount of Lintao County.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed governor of Yan Province; soon he was given the seal of opening an office and separately enfeoffed viscount of Lintao County.

literal: In the third year, together with various generals he campaigned south against the Yangtze and Huai regions and captured Yangping Commandery.
idiomatic: In the third year, together with other generals, he campaigned south into the Yangtze and Huai country and captured Yangping Commandery.

literal: When Chen forces besieged Guangling, an edict made Ping command all armies south of the river in relief; the Chen forces withdrew, and he then returned.
idiomatic: When Chen forces besieged Guangling, an edict put Ping in command of all armies south of the river for relief; the Chen men withdrew, and he returned.

literal: In summer of the fifth year he died in the province, aged fifty-one.
idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year he died in office, aged fifty-one.

literal: Posthumously granted military affairs of the three provinces of Ying, Cang, and You, governor of Ying Province, and director of the Palace Secretary; posthumous title Zhuanghui.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted military affairs over Ying, Cang, and You provinces, governor of Ying Province, and director of the palace secretary; posthumous title Zhuanghui.

literal: His son Xiaozhong succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Xiaozhong succeeded.

literal: His younger brother Changyi.
idiomatic: His younger brother Changyi.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was palace attendant, grand master equal in rank to the Three Excellencies with an office, enfeoffed Prince of Xining.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was palace attendant, grand master equal in rank to the three excellencies with an office, and enfeoffed prince of Xining.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was pillar of state and died as chief administrator of Jing Province.
idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was pillar of state and died while serving as chief administrator of Jing Province.

literal: Though he possessed no other special skill, in earlier service he was renowned for integrity and efficiency.
idiomatic: Though he had no other special talent, in earlier service he was known for integrity and efficiency.

literal: Buda Hansa
idiomatic: Buda Hansa

literal: Buda Hansa was a man of Dina in Taian.
idiomatic: Buda Hansa was a man of Dina in Taian.

literal: His great-grandfather Rong served Wei and successively held the governorships of the two commanderies of Jinmen and Huazheng.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong served Wei and in turn held the governorships of Jinmen and Huazheng.

literal: His father Ju was General of Soaring Dragon and separate commander of tribally enrolled forces.
idiomatic: His father Ju was general of soaring dragon and separate commander of tribally enrolled forces.

literal: At the end of Zhengguang the Six Garrisons rose in rebellion; Hansa then led his family south to seek refuge and went to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.
idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang the Six Garrisons rose in rebellion; Hansa led his family south to seek refuge and went to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.

literal: Later he followed Rong into Luoyang and, for military merit, was appointed camp commander within the Yangwu Army, enfeoffed Viscount of Jiangxia.
idiomatic: Later he followed Rong into Luoyang and, for military merit, was appointed camp commander within the Yangwu Army and enfeoffed viscount of Jiangxia.

literal: He followed in pacifying Ge Rong; accumulating his successive merits, he was made General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: He followed in the pacification of Ge Rong; with merit accumulated over many campaigns, he was made general who pacifies the south.

literal: After Rong died, he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang, was appointed grand commander within the camp, and followed Zhao in resisting battle at Hanling.
idiomatic: After Rong died, he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang, was appointed grand commander within the camp, and followed Zhao in resisting at Hanling.

literal: When Zhao was defeated, Hansa surrendered with the force under his command.
idiomatic: When Zhao was defeated, Hansa surrendered with the troops under his command.

literal: The Grand Ancestor made him third tribally enrolled chieftain; he was successively promoted to garrison commander of Qin Province's fort and governor of Northern Yong Province.
idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor made him third tribally enrolled chieftain; he rose in stages to garrison commander of Qin Province's fort and governor of Northern Yong Province.

literal: During Tianping he was transferred to area commander of the three springs of Eastern Shouyang.
idiomatic: During Tianping he was transferred to area commander of the three springs of Eastern Shouyang.

literal: During Yuanxiang he acted as governor of Yan Province; he was successively promoted to grand commander of tribally enrolled forces of Linchuan and enfeoffed Baron of Changguang.
idiomatic: During Yuanxiang he acted as governor of Yan Province; he rose in stages to grand commander of tribally enrolled forces of Linchuan and was enfeoffed baron of Changguang.

literal: At that time the Rouran raided and plundered, repeatedly doing border harm; the Grand Ancestor soothed and received them and dispatched Hansa to carry the mission.
idiomatic: At that time the Rouran raided the borders again and again; the Grand Ancestor sought to soothe and win them over and dispatched Hansa on the mission.

literal: On his return he was appointed equal in rank to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On his return he was appointed equal in rank to the three excellencies.

literal: He went out as grand commander of Wucheng and garrisoned Heyang.
idiomatic: He went out as grand commander of Wucheng and garrisoned Heyang.

literal: He was additionally made grand general of chariots and cavalry and given an office; his enfeoffment was advanced to Duke of Xingtang County, with three hundred households from Bohai reduced to augment his fief.
idiomatic: He was additionally made grand general of chariots and cavalry and given an office; his enfeoffment was advanced to duke of Xingtang County, with three hundred households from Bohai taken to augment his fief.

literal: He was then appointed governor of Jin Province, separately enfeoffed Baron of Anling County with a fief of two hundred households, and made grand general of fast cavalry.
idiomatic: He was then appointed governor of Jin Province, separately enfeoffed baron of Anling County with a fief of two hundred households, and made grand general of fast cavalry.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yiyang Commandery.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his enfeoffment was changed to duke of Yiyang Commandery.

literal: Murong Yan
idiomatic: Murong Yan

literal: Murong Yan, styled Shide, was a man of Cheng'an in Qingdu and a descendant of Murong Hui.
idiomatic: Murong Yan, styled Shide, was a man of Cheng'an in Qingdu and a descendant of Murong Hui.

literal: His father Chitou was governor of Nandun in Wei; he stood ten chi in height, his belt nine chi long.
idiomatic: His father Chitou had been governor of Nandun in Wei — a man ten chi tall, with a belt nine chi long.

literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was posthumously granted grand master equal in rank to the Three Excellencies with an office, left vice director of the masters of writing, bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs of Cang and Heng provinces, and governor of Heng Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuping he was posthumously granted grand master equal in rank to the three excellencies with an office, left vice director of the masters of writing, bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs over Cang and Heng provinces, and governor of Heng Province.

literal: Yan's appearance surpassed the crowd; his bearing in cap and robes was very imposing. He did not care for reading books but studied military arts considerably and was skilled at horsemanship and archery.
idiomatic: Yan's looks stood out from the crowd; in cap and robes he cut an imposing figure. He cared little for books but studied the art of war and was skilled at horsemanship and archery.

literal: During Zhengguang, Prince Hejian of Wei Yuanchen led troops to relieve Shouyang and summoned Yan as commander of the left wing; for battle merit he was rewarded with fifty bolts of silk.
idiomatic: During Zhengguang, Prince Hejian of Wei, Yuanchen, led troops to relieve Shouyang and summoned Yan as commander of the left wing; for battle merit he was rewarded with fifty bolts of silk.

literal: The army halted at West Xiashi; thereby he relieved the siege of Woyang and pacified Cangling City and the Jingshan garrison.
idiomatic: The army halted at West Xiashi; there he lifted the siege of Woyang and pacified Cangling City and the Jingshan garrison.

literal: Liang dispatched General Zheng Seng and others to offer battle; Yan attacked them, beheaded their general Xiao Qiao, and the Liang men fled in rout.
idiomatic: Liang dispatched General Zheng Seng and others to offer battle; Yan struck them, beheaded their general Xiao Qiao, and the Liang men broke and fled.

literal: Again he launched a surprise attack and broke the army of Wang Shennian and others, capturing more than two hundred men; Shennian barely escaped with his life.
idiomatic: Again he launched a surprise attack and broke the army of Wang Shennian and others, taking more than two hundred prisoners; Shennian barely escaped with his life.

literal: In the third year Liang dispatched generals to attack Eastern Yu Province; Grand Commander Yuan Baozhang campaigned against them.
idiomatic: In the third year Liang dispatched generals against Eastern Yu Province; Grand Commander Yuan Baozhang was sent to repel them.

literal: Yan served as separate commander.
idiomatic: Yan served as separate commander.

literal: At Zhenghai he joined battle, beheading their army commander Zhu Sengzhen and deputy army commander Qin Tai.
idiomatic: At Zhenghai he joined battle and beheaded their army commander Zhu Sengzhen and deputy army commander Qin Tai.

literal: Again he struck the bandit Wang Gou at Yangxia and pacified him.
idiomatic: Again he struck the bandit Wang Gou at Yangxia and pacified him.

literal: During Xiaochang, Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and appointed Yan southern commander of the capital region.
idiomatic: During Xiaochang, Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and appointed Yan southern commander of the capital region.

literal: During Yong'an, Western Jing Province was besieged by the Liang general Cao Yizong; Yan answered the call and went to its aid.
idiomatic: During Yong'an, Western Jing Province was besieged by the Liang general Cao Yizong; Yan answered the call and marched to its relief.

literal: At that time the governor of Beiyu, Song Daijian, plotted rebellion; Yan then led light cavalry by surprise, going straight to the foot of the city wall, and said: "The great army has already arrived — why does the governor not come out to greet them?
idiomatic: At that time the governor of Beiyu, Song Daijian, plotted rebellion; Yan led light cavalry by surprise straight to the foot of the wall and called out: "The great army has already arrived — why does the governor not come out to greet us?

literal: " Daijian, startled and terrified, knew not what to do and thereupon came out to greet him; Yan immediately seized him, and the whole commandery was settled.
idiomatic: " Startled and at a loss, Daijian came out to greet him; Yan seized him on the spot, and the whole commandery was settled.

literal: Again he broke the Liang generals Ma Yuanda, Cai Tianqi, and Liu Baijia, accumulating merit time and again.
idiomatic: Again he broke the Liang generals Ma Yuanda, Cai Tianqi, and Liu Baijia, winning merit again and again.

literal: He was appointed General of Powerful Crossbows.
idiomatic: He was appointed general of powerful crossbows.

literal: Joining battle with the Liang generals Wang Xuanzhen, Dong Dangmen, and others, he broke them all, relieved the siege of Rang City, and recovered Nanyang and Xinyi.
idiomatic: Joining battle with the Liang generals Wang Xuanzhen, Dong Dangmen, and others, he broke them all, lifted the siege of Rang City, and recovered Nanyang and Xinyi.

literal: He was transferred to General of Accumulated Shots, bearer of the staff of authority, and grand commander of fortification defense in Yu Province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to general of accumulated shots, bearer of the staff of authority, and grand commander of fortification defense in Yu Province.

literal: When the Erzhu clan was defeated, together with Governor Li En of Yu Province he submitted to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: When the Erzhu clan fell, he and Governor Li En of Yu Province submitted to the Grand Ancestor.

literal: For successive merits he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Gaoliang, transferred to governor of Wucheng and governor of Eastern Yong Province.
idiomatic: For successive merits he was promoted to general who pacifies the east and governor of Gaoliang, then transferred to governor of Wucheng and governor of Eastern Yong Province.

literal: After the defeat at Shaye, Guo Luan, governor of Jing Province in Western Wei, led troops to attack Yan; Yan held out in defense for more than two hundred days, fighting day and night at full strength; he inflicted a great defeat on Luan's army, pursued and beheaded more than three hundred men, and again captured Guo Ta, governor of Western Wei.
idiomatic: After the defeat at Shaye, Guo Luan, governor of Jing Province in Western Wei, led troops against Yan; Yan held the city for more than two hundred days, fighting day and night without rest; he broke Luan's army utterly, pursued and beheaded more than three hundred men, and captured Guo Ta, another Western Wei governor.

literal: At that time many provinces turned and fell, but Yan alone remained intact.
idiomatic: At that time many provinces turned and fell, but Yan alone held firm.
